title: How the Go SDK builds requests and interprets responses: client options, bodies, status codes, bulk deletes
aliases: object returned from api was not a pointer

prose.text: These are claims about the Go SDK (the same client whose retries are in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]])'s request and response handling, shared by the Terraform providers built on it. They are about what the client does with options, bodies and status codes.

prose.label: Proxy options in providers.
prose.text: {{providers-append-proxy-after-rebuilds}} Whether a configured proxy is used for service requests is open {{gap:proxy-effect}}.

prose.label: Create responses.
prose.text: {{ztw-create-requires-exact-content-type}} {{ztw-create-type-assert-fails-after-post}} {{zia-create-same-exact-content-type}} Whether the APIs send the parameterized content types or empty bodies that trigger these is open {{gap:server-response-shapes}}. The same post-write failure is described in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]].
Two retry-loop details are not covered by [[shared.sdk-go.retries]]. {{retry-paths-replace-body-without-closing}} {{retry-sleeps-ignore-cancellation}}
Related: empty-body handling for ZIA updates is in [[zia.sdk-go.write-encoding]]; token handling in [[shared.sdk-go.auth-lifecycle]]; response caching in [[shared.sdk-go.cache]].

checks.do: Whether traffic from a provider meant to use a proxy reaches the proxy, rather than trusting the provider's http_proxy setting.
Whether a failed ZTC or ZIA create was accepted by the tenant before retrying it.

clients-built-before-options.statement: `NewConfiguration` builds every per-service HTTP client (`setHttpClients`) before it applies the caller's option functions. Options therefore see clients that already exist, and only the options that call `setHttpClients` again rebuild them.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

proxy-and-tls-options-only-set-fields.statement: `WithProxyHost`, `WithProxyPort`, `WithProxyUsername`, `WithProxyPassword` and `WithTestingDisableHttpsCheck` only assign configuration fields; they do not rebuild any client. The proxy and TLS-skip settings are read once, inside `getHTTPClient`, when a client is built. A setter that runs after the last client build leaves the live transport on the default proxy-from-environment behavior.

quotes: proxyFunc := http.ProxyFromEnvironment // Default behavior (uses system/env variables)

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

rate-and-timeout-options-rebuild-clients.statement: `WithRequestTimeout`, `WithRateLimitMaxRetries`, `WithRateLimitMinWait`, `WithRateLimitMaxWait` and `WithRateLimitRemainingThreshold` each call `setHttpClients` again, building fresh clients from the configuration as it stands at that moment. Whether proxy and TLS options take effect therefore depends on whether one of these runs after them.

custom-http-client-not-used-for-service-.statement: A client passed with `WithHttpClientPtr` is stored only as the generic client, and any later rebuilding option overwrites it. Requests to ZIA, ZPA, ZCC, ZTW and ZDX endpoints use the per-service clients chosen by `getServiceHTTPClient`, so a caller-supplied client reaches only the default and admin routes.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

providers-append-proxy-after-rebuilds.statement: In the OneAPI option list of each audited provider (ZIA, ZPA, ZTC, ZCC), the proxy options are appended after the timeout and rate-limit options that rebuild the clients, and none of the four sets the TLS-skip option. The configured proxy host and port are therefore recorded in the configuration but absent from the transports that carry service requests; a proxy set through the standard environment variables is unaffected, because the transport defaults to reading them. The SDK's own `ZSCALER_CLIENT_PROXY_HOST` and `ZSCALER_CLIENT_PROXY_PORT` environment variables are read before the first client build and do take effect, and the default transport still honors `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`; only the proxy passed through the provider's configuration is lost.
providers-append-proxy-after-rebuilds.conditions: Rests on the order of entries in each provider's setter slice (applied in order by `NewConfiguration`) and on a search for the TLS option: `git -C vendor/<provider> grep -n 'DisableHttpsCheck\|InsecureSkipVerify' <tag> -- '*.go'` returns nothing outside tests for tf-zia v4.8.3, tf-zpa v4.4.10, tf-ztc v0.2.0 and tf-zcc v0.1.0-beta.1. Not observed against a running proxy. The per-product legacy clients under zscaler/zpa, zscaler/zia and zscaler/ztw have their own option functions and were not traced.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zcc-request-do-double-marshals.statement: `NewZccRequestDo` JSON-marshals its `body` argument unconditionally on the OneAPI (non-legacy) path, and four SDK methods (admin-user update, both entitlement updates, manage-pass update) pass it a `bytes.NewBuffer` of bytes they have already marshaled. A `*bytes.Buffer` has no exported fields, so it marshals as `{}`, and the request carries an empty object instead of the payload.
zcc-request-do-double-marshals.conditions: The `{}` result is Go standard-library behavior, reproduced locally with `json.Marshal(bytes.NewBuffer(...))`; no request was sent. What the ZCC API does with a `{}` body is server behavior and was not tested.

evidence.after: func (client *Client) NewZccRequestDo(ctx context.Context, method, endpoint string, options, body, v interface{}) (*http.Response, error) {

quotes: resp, err := service.Client.NewZccRequestDo(ctx, "POST", managePassEndpoint, nil, bytes.NewBuffer(body), nil)
resp, err := service.Client.NewZccRequestDo(ctx, "PUT", editAdminUserEndpoint, nil, bytes.NewBuffer(body), nil)

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zcc-double-marshal-not-reached-by-provid.statement: The audited ZCC provider build does not call the affected methods, so the double-marshal is reached only by code that calls those SDK functions directly.
zcc-double-marshal-not-reached-by-provid.conditions: Absence: `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zcc grep -n 'entitlements\|manage_pass\|UpdateAdminUser' v0.1.0-beta.1 -- '*.go'` returns no match, and the only `admin_users` use is the read-only `GetAdminUsers` in internal/framework/datasources/admin_user.go. Other SDK callers (for example the zscalerctl tool) were not searched. In the SDK, `git grep 'NewZccRequestDo(.*bytes\.' v3.8.37 -- zscaler/zcc zscaler/zpa` lists exactly these four call sites.

request-do-fabricates-200.statement: The ZPA, ZCC and ZDX request helpers discard the response object that `ExecuteRequest` returns and build a new `http.Response` holding only `StatusCode: 200` and the body. A 201, 202 or 204 reaches the caller as 200, and response headers are lost.

quotes: respBody, _, _, err := client.ExecuteRequest(ctx, method, endpoint, bodyReader, nil, contentTypeJSON)
respBody, _, _, err := client.ExecuteRequest(ctx, method, endpoint, bodyReader, nil, contentTypeJSON)

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

fabricated-200-disables-status-checks.statement: Because the wrapper always reports 200, status checks written after it, such as the ZCC service methods' `resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK` guards, can never fire. A real failure status is already turned into an error inside `ExecuteRequest`, so the guard adds nothing; a success status other than 200 is indistinguishable from 200.
fabricated-200-disables-status-checks.conditions: Depends on `ExecuteRequest` returning an error for statuses of 300 and above, which is read from its retry loop (`if resp.StatusCode < 300 { break }` followed by error returns) and not exercised. ZPA service code was searched for status comparisons at v3.8.42 and only its tests compare status codes.

empty-success-body-decoded-as-eof.statement: When a caller passes a decode target and the response body is empty (such as a 204), the ZPA, ZCC and ZDX wrappers still run the decoder over zero bytes, which returns `io.EOF`; the wrapper returns that as an error even though the request succeeded.
empty-success-body-decoded-as-eof.conditions: The `io.EOF` result is Go standard-library behavior for `json.NewDecoder(...).Decode` on empty input, reproduced locally. It is reached only when a server answers a call that has a non-nil decode target with an empty body; which ZPA and ZCC endpoints do so is server behavior and was not traced per endpoint.

quotes: if err := decodeJSON(respBody, v); err != nil {
if err := decodeJSON(respBody, v); err != nil {

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

ztw-create-requires-exact-content-type.statement: ZTW `CreateResource` decodes the response into the typed object only when the `Content-Type` header equals `application/json` exactly (case-insensitive). Any other value, including a valid `application/json; charset=utf-8`, takes the else branch, which returns the raw `*http.Response` with a nil error.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

ztw-create-type-assert-fails-after-post.statement: ZTW service create methods type-assert the value `CreateResource` returns. If the response header did not match exactly, the assertion fails and the method returns an error after the POST was already sent, so the caller sees a failed create for a request the server may have accepted.
ztw-create-type-assert-fails-after-post.conditions: Needs the ZTC API to send a `Content-Type` with parameters (or any value other than exactly `application/json`) on create responses, which is server behavior and not shown by the SDK. 18 ZTW service files call `CreateResource` (`git grep -l 'Client.CreateResource(ctx' v3.8.40 -- zscaler/ztw`); two were read in full. ZTC provider v0.2.0 builds on v3.8.40.

zia-create-same-exact-content-type.statement: The ZIA `Create` helper has the same exact-match `Content-Type` comparison and the same raw-response fallback, and ZIA service create methods type-assert its result the same way. The ZIA provider builds on v3.8.44 and reaches it wherever its resources call these service create methods (75 files use `Client.Create`, not individually traced).
zia-create-same-exact-content-type.conditions: The comparison is quoted; the type assertion was read in one ZIA service (url categories). `git grep -l 'Client.Create(ctx' v3.8.44 -- zscaler/zia` lists 75 files, none of which were individually checked. Whether the ZIA API sends a parameterized `Content-Type` on create is server behavior and was not tested.

bulk-delete-rejects-nonempty-success.statement: The ZTW `BulkDeleteResource` and ZIA `BulkDelete` helpers treat any nonempty body after a successful request as an error: they return a 200 response together with an "unexpected response" error. Only an empty body counts as success.

evidence.after: func (c *Client) BulkDeleteResource(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, payload interface{}) (*http.Response, error) {
func (c *Client) BulkDelete(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, payload interface{}) (*http.Response, error) {

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

bulk-delete-helpers-reach.statement: Nothing in the ZTW services calls `BulkDeleteResource`, and the ZTC provider does not either, so that helper is reached only by direct SDK callers. ZIA's `BulkDelete` is called by three ZIA service helpers (locations, VPN credentials, users); the ZIA provider's only use is a sweeper test, not a resource.
bulk-delete-helpers-reach.conditions: Absence searches: `git -C vendor/zscaler-sdk-go grep -n 'BulkDelete' v3.8.40 -- zscaler/ztw` (only the legacy client's own method), `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-ztc grep -n 'BulkDelete' v0.2.0 -- '*.go'` (none), and `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zia grep -n 'BulkDelete' v4.8.3 -- '*.go'` (only zia/provider_sweeper_test.go). ZPA has its own bulk-delete helpers on `NewRequestDo` that were not traced here.

bulk-delete-helpers-truncate-ids.statement: Three ZIA bulk-delete helpers cut the ID list to a local maximum (100 for locations and VPN credentials, 500 for users) and send only the first IDs. They return no error and do not chunk the rest; the only trace is an INFO log line. The users helper's comment says "first 100" while its constant is 500.

quotes: // Truncate the list to the first 100 IDs

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

bulk-delete-truncation-scope.statement: Those three are the only ID-list truncations found in the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC and ZTW services, and no provider resource calls them: the ZIA provider's one caller is a sweeper test that batches the IDs itself.
bulk-delete-truncation-scope.conditions: Absence: `git -C vendor/zscaler-sdk-go grep -n 'ids\[:\|IDs\[:' v3.8.44 -- zscaler` returns only the three lines quoted above; slicing under other variable names was not searched. Direct SDK callers (scripts, other tools) are the exposed population.

retry-paths-replace-body-without-closing.statement: In the 401, edit-lock (409/412) and 403 LIMIT_EXCEEDED branches of the outer retry loop, the SDK reads the response body with `io.ReadAll`, then replaces `resp.Body` with an in-memory reader without closing the original. Only the final success path drains and closes the body (`tryDrainBody`). Whether this holds connections open depends on the transport, since the body was read to its end.
retry-paths-replace-body-without-closing.conditions: Absence of a `Close` in those branches: `git show v3.8.44:zscaler/oneapiconfig.go | grep -n 'Body.Close\|NopCloser\|tryDrainBody'` shows one `Body.Close` (inside the retryablehttp `ErrorHandler` in `getHTTPClient`) and one `tryDrainBody` (on the success path). No leak was measured; Go's HTTP/1 transport can reuse a connection once the body is read to EOF, so the practical effect is unproven. Retry behavior itself is in shared.sdk-go.retries.

evidence.after: // ✅ Check for session invalidation errors in 401 responses

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK client lifecycle) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

retry-sleeps-ignore-cancellation.statement: The outer retry loop waits with plain `time.Sleep` in its rate-limit, edit-lock, 5xx and session-refresh branches. The rate-limit branch checks the context before it sleeps, but none of the sleeps can be cut short, so cancellation is noticed only after the wait ends.

evidence.after: // Check if context is still valid before sleeping
// Check if this is an EDIT_LOCK_NOT_AVAILABLE / org barrier error

proxy-effect.title: Whether a provider-configured proxy is actually used for service requests
proxy-effect.blocks: saying a configured http_proxy is bypassed in practice, rather than predicted from option order
proxy-effect.detail: Run a provider build through a logging proxy with http_proxy set and the standard proxy environment variables unset, and see whether service requests arrive at the proxy.

server-response-shapes.title: What Content-Type and success bodies the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC and ZTC APIs send
server-response-shapes.blocks: saying whether the exact Content-Type match, the empty-body decode and the bulk-delete body check ever fail against a real tenant
server-response-shapes.detail: Capture raw create, delete and bulk-delete responses (status, Content-Type header, body) per endpoint; the SDK paths fail only for a parameterized Content-Type, an empty body with a decode target, or a nonempty bulk-delete body.
